subsystems.name: Ribbon tether
subsystems.role: the cable itself, extending from the equator to beyond geostationary orbit, held taut by Earth's rotation.

subsystems.name: Anchor platform
subsystems.role: holds the lower end at the equator, usually a mobile ocean platform to avoid storms and allow slight movement.

subsystems.name: Counterweight
subsystems.role: a mass placed beyond geostationary orbit to keep the ribbon under tension.

subsystems.name: Climber
subsystems.role: a robotic car that grips the ribbon and carries payloads up and down.

subsystems.name: Power delivery
subsystems.role: supplies energy to climbers, since they cannot carry enough fuel for the whole trip.

subsystems.name: Debris and traffic management
subsystems.role: protects the ribbon from impacts, which could sever it.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the material
buildSteps.detail: Grow carbon nanotubes or boron-nitride nanotubes with near-perfect atomic structure and lengths far beyond today's centimetre-scale samples.

buildSteps.title: Spin into fibres
buildSteps.detail: Align the nanotubes into macroscopic fibres and measure their specific strength (strength per unit density).

buildSteps.title: Weave the ribbon
buildSteps.detail: Braid fibres into a wide, thin ribbon, designed with a taper so stress is uniform from the ground to beyond geostationary orbit.

buildSteps.title: Deploy a seed ribbon
buildSteps.detail: Launch a small seed ribbon to geostationary orbit, then lower a pilot line toward Earth while raising a small counterweight.

buildSteps.title: Anchor and tension
buildSteps.detail: Secure the lower end to a mobile ocean platform at the equator and adjust tension so the ribbon remains stable.

buildSteps.title: Build up the full ribbon
buildSteps.detail: Send climbers up and down, adding more strands until the ribbon reaches its design strength.

buildSteps.title: Install the counterweight
buildSteps.detail: Position a large mass beyond geostationary orbit to balance the downward pull of the lower section.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Climbers carry payloads to orbit; robots inspect and repair the ribbon continuously.

prerequisites.why: the ribbon must be roughly an order of magnitude stronger per unit weight than any engineering fibre available today.
a single atomic defect can start a crack that tears the whole ribbon; no process yet makes metre-scale perfect fibres.
climbers need energy for the multi-day climb to geostationary orbit; laser and microwave beaming have been demonstrated only at low power.
the ribbon is a huge, thin target; impacts at orbital speed could sever it.
spacecraft already reach and operate in geostationary orbit, where deployment would begin.

pathway.milestone: laboratory fibres with strengths far below the requirement; fundamental materials research
pathway.unlocks: a clearer picture of which nanotube or boron-nitride route is most promising.

pathway.milestone: metre-scale ribbon samples tested in vacuum and under radiation
pathway.unlocks: confidence that a long ribbon can survive the space environment.

pathway.milestone: subscale orbital demonstration: a tether a few kilometres long deployed from a spacecraft
pathway.unlocks: data on deployment, stability and debris avoidance.

pathway.milestone: full-scale seed ribbon and gradual build-up to a complete elevator
pathway.unlocks: routine, low-cost transport to geostationary orbit and beyond.
